text:
Maggie: Heads up — Riverbank wants to swap from CompCorp API to Redwood for generation + embeddings. They asked for a short POC to validate deep response deltas, function-call parity, and billing equivalence. Can we outline a preflight test plan and surface any enterprise blockers?
Omar: Do we have their expected qps/seq-len distribution? that will drive batching/throughput advice.
Maggie: Sales note says bursty read-heavy (200 RPS peak, 5–20 token median,/outliers up to 8k). Lots of small embedding calls too.
Jin: Main risk is function-calling differences and the way CompCorp encodes multi-part responses. They rely on a custom header for streaming chunks. Need to confirm our streaming+fncall mapping.
Tolga: Tokenization delta is often the silent cost driver. CompCorp uses BPE variant that tokenizes some suffixes differently => they billed less per-sample historically. We should include a small tokenizer parity check. Sample shim we use in presales:```bash
# quick curl to map headers
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "X-Client-Mode: compat" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","prompt":"Hello"}'
```
Jin: Also test function-call name/arg normalization. Example delta we saw: CompCorp returned `function_call.name":"get_price_v1"` while Redwood returns `get_price`. Some customers rely on exact names in their router. We'll need a translation table or aliasing shim.
Sara: I can run the parity eval—proposed test matrix: 1) prompt parity (1000 prompts), 2) function-call mapping (50 fncases), 3) streaming chunking (10 long sessions), 4) tokenizer token-count diff (samples), 5) billing estimator. ETA 3 business days for initial run.
Sales-Eng: For pricing Qs, they asked how embeddings map to token billing when they batch many small texts. Recommend we propose a blended rate for bulk embedding traffic + an embedding-cache suggestion. I'll draft a cost model.
sec-bot: Security checklist reminder — Riverbank requires SOC2 + an external pen test report and answers to a 120-question vendor security questionnaire. Standard SLA addendum + KMS support requested. 72h turnaround for questionnaire expected.
Tolga: Potential enterprise blocker: in their legal template they want data residency restrictions and guaranteed cache eviction windows. That maps to Private deployment ask. Flagging for AE and Solutions.
Maggie: Good notes. Action items:
- Sara: run parity eval (due in 3 days).
- Sales-Eng: draft blended pricing + embedding cache recommendation (2 days).
- Jin/Tolga: produce fn-call alias table and tokenizer diff sample (2 days).
- Omar: verify required throughput on Redwood Dedicated and advise scaling policy for bursty 200 RPS.
- Security team: I'll ping sec-ops about the questionnaire and pen test artifacts.
Maggie: Ping me in-thread with any hard-blockers. :thumbsup:
Omar: :eyes: starting capacity calc now.
Jin: I'll stub alias table and drop sample responses here when ready.
Sara: kicking off eval now — will post preliminary summary in 24–36h.
Sales-Eng: working on cost model, will attach an excel mock.
sec-bot: Noted. Addendum: please upload requested certs to the vendor portal (link sent by email).
